text:
alex: FYI customer (tenant: tenant-acme) is missing ~12 audit events in their SIEM for a 30m window yesterday. They see a manifest with all files uploaded but the SIEM only ingested a subset.

maria: can you paste the export_job_id and one manifest entry? also is this the splunk HEC connector or a customer-managed forwarder?

alex: export_job_id=job_2026_03_16_23_41_07
alex: manifest sample: 

```
{"s3_key": "audit/tenant-acme/2026-03-16/23/41/part-0003.gz", "kms_alias": "alias/redwood-audit-prod", "size": 1048576}
```

alex: customer is using our splunk HEC forwarder (SaaS) not their own. They pointed out missing events are all identity-change events.

audit-bot: export-job job_2026_03_16_23_41_07 retried 3 times, last status=partial_success, error=KMS_DECRYPT_ERROR on 2 files

tyler: KMS_DECRYPT_ERROR could cause files to be skipped by the forwarder. do we have a recent KMS alias rotation? I remember a rotation window around 2026-03-16.

maria: checking rotation logs now. alex — can you run a quick sanity: download one of the files and attempt local decrypt with the alias and report error? if it's a perm decryption problem we need infra to re-encrypt or replay.

alex: ran `aws s3 cp s3://redwood-audit-prod/audit/tenant-acme/2026-03-16/23/41/part-0003.gz ./ && kms-cli decrypt --alias alias/redwood-audit-prod part-0003.gz` -> returns: 

```
ERROR: KMS Decrypt failed: AccessDeniedException: arn:aws:kms:us-west-2:123456:key/xxxx
```

alex: but other parts (part-0001, part-0002) decrypt fine. so it's inconsistent.

kevin: AccessDenied on specific object usually points to envelope key id mismatch after rewrap or partial re-encrypt. There was a backfill that re-keyed some partitions last week. Could be a race where the manifest references an old key id.

maria: can you share the object metadata for part-0003? `aws s3api head-object --bucket redwood-audit-prod --key "audit/tenant-acme/2026-03-16/23/41/part-0003.gz" --query Metadata`

alex: metadata shows: `{ "kms-key-id": "arn:aws:kms:us-west-2:123456:key/old-key", "tenant-id": "tenant-acme" }`

tyler: that confirms it. forwarder attempted decryption with current alias but object encrypted with old-key. If old-key was scheduled for retirement that could cause AccessDenied.

maria: next steps: 1) infra to restore access to old-key (allow decrypt for service account) 2) replay job for affected manifest entries 3) confirm SIEM dedup logic — ensure replay doesn't create duplicates for already-ingested events.

kevin: on dedup: Splunk HEC connector uses dedup by event_id in payload. If payloads lack identity fields or event_id was stripped by transformation we could both miss and duplicate. alex: can you sample one of the records from part-0003 and show the top-level keys?

alex: extracted one line from decompressed part-0003.gz (after we temporarily rewrapped key locally): 

```
{"ts": "2026-03-16T23:41:12Z", "event_type": "identity.change", "user": {"id": "u-123"}, "tenant_id": "tenant-acme", "event_id": "evt-9b7"}
```

alex: records contain event_id and tenant_id. interestingly, customer said SIEM shows duplicates for evt-9b7 in a different timebucket (23:40).

tyler: timebucket mismatch could be due to gz rotation boundary or our batching sending with wrong timestamp header. check forwarder logs for publish timestamps around 23:40-23:42.

maria: forwarding logs for job_2026_03_16_23_41_07: 

```
[23:41:10] publish to splunk.hec 200 payload_size=71234 events=120
[23:41:10] publish to splunk.hec 200 payload_size=80521 events=134
[23:41:45] publish to splunk.hec 200 payload_size=60000 events=110
[23:42:02] publish to splunk.hec 500 error=payload_too_large
[23:42:10] publish to splunk.hec 200 payload_size=12000 events=25
```
maria: we see one 500 around 23:42 which triggered a retry; retry logic uses last-known-batch-timestamp which might have been set to 23:40 in one code path — could explain duplicates at 23:40 bucket.

kevin: ok action items: infra to re-grant decrypt on old-key for service principal (owner: infra@redwood), eng-runtime to patch forwarder to avoid reusing stale batch timestamps during retries (owner: tyler), support to coordinate replay and ensure customer dedup configured (owner: maria).

alex: I did a manual replay of part-0003 via our backfill tool against a non-prod splunk endpoint and verified it ingests without duplicates when dedup header present. command used: 

```
./backfill --job job_2026_03_16_23_41_07 --file s3://redwood-audit-prod/audit/tenant-acme/2026-03-16/23/41/part-0003.gz --target splunk-nonprod
```

alex: non-prod replay showed the 12 missing events arrive in correct bucket. customer agreed to a replay after infra fixes.

maria: thanks. i've opened a tracking ticket ENGSEC-2481 and cc'd infra/splunk-team. i'll update customer with timeline: infra fix + replay window (approx 2 hours).

kevin: please attach the object metadata and forwarder logs to the ticket. and note whether the KMS key rotation window overlapped with the export job — that'll be important for compliance audit.

alex: attaching logs to ENGSEC-2481 now. will follow up when infra confirms old-key access restored. :thumbsup:
